title: Does AI rate through the cycle? — reproducibility artifact
description: Reproducibility artifact for the Finance Research Letters submission Does AI rate through the cycle? — the first controlled measurement of procyclicality in credit assessment. Firm fundamentals are held byte-identical across an ordered five-point macroeconomic-severity axis (plus a matched credit-irrelevant placebo axis), so any rating movement is procyclicality by construction. From a frozen 32,000-rating dataset (5 frontier LLMs × 4 prompt framings × 80 synthetic firms × 10 macro/placebo states × 2 seeds) the analysis regenerates the cyclicality coefficient (notches per severity step) with firm-clustered bootstrap 95% CIs, the boom-to-recession swing, the downside/upside asymmetry, the Amato–Furfine ordered-probit null, the log-probability expected-notch estimator, the placebo-adjusted (net) coefficient, and the through-the-cycle vs 'be stable' instruction contrasts. The reproducible run is offline, deterministic and free; live model capture (vendor API keys) is intentionally excluded.
notes: Code released under MIT (see LICENSE); data, analysis outputs and text under CC-BY-4.0. Affiliation, ORCID, related-publication DOI and repository URL to be completed at deposit. Live-capture SDKs (openai, google-genai) are not required to reproduce results from the frozen data.
